clue.text: State of rabbit regularly engulfed by tidal water

indicators.note: something engulfed by water is swallowed up inside it, so the picked letters go within

parts.note: the sea is the tidal water

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, the first, third and fifth of the word rabbit

explanation.surface: A rabbit keeps being swamped by the incoming tide.
explanation.definitionFit: Serbia is a sovereign country in the Balkans, and a country is a state.

clue.text: Behind time, jettisoning first of boosters over the moon

indicators.note: throwing off, as a rocket sheds its stages, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: belated means late, behind time

indicators.note: points to the first letter of boosters

explanation.surface: A rocket launched late sheds its first booster on its way to the moon.
explanation.definitionFit: Over the moon is an idiom for delighted, thrilled.

clue.text: Financial adviser's source of healthy food?

definitions.meaning: a slang, slightly mocking term for an accountant
humorously, a shop counter selling pulses

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is an idiom for an accountant and, read literally, a counter where beans are sold.
explanation.definitionFit: Bean counter is informal for an accountant obsessed with figures; literally it could be a stall where healthy beans come from.

clue.text: Vegetable poisonous types take in a meat and tomato sauce

indicators.note: the snakes take in the letters, holding them inside

parts.note: asps are venomous snakes
ragu is an Italian meat and tomato sauce

explanation.surface: Poisonous kinds of veg absorb a bolognese sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Asparagus is a vegetable eaten for its young green spears.

clue.text: Cute American kid, one abandoned by German city family

indicators.note: the city leaves behind the letter for one, so it is dropped from the name

parts.note: Munich is a city in Bavaria, Germany
I is the Roman numeral for one
kin means family or relatives

explanation.surface: A sweet young American is left behind by a family from a German city.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage a munchkin is an affectionate word for a small child, after the little people of The Wizard of Oz.

clue.text: Conductors from West maybe on second short tour

parts.note: Mae West was the American actress, an example of a Mae

indicators.note: short means missing its last letter, so the tour is cut off at the end

parts.note: a trip is a tour

explanation.surface: Orchestra conductors from the West go on a short second tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West' looks like a direction; it is the actress Mae West.
explanation.definitionFit: Maestri is the Italian plural of maestro, a title given to distinguished orchestral conductors.

clue.text: Finally bitten by a bloodsucking fly, being bald

indicators.note: finally points to the final letter of bitten

parts.note: a ked is a wingless bloodsucking fly that lives on sheep

explanation.surface: Someone without hair is at last bitten by a bloodsucking insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Bald in the sense of plain and unadorned, as in the bald truth, means bare or naked.

clue.text: A woman's idol? Not altogether

indicators.note: not altogether means not complete, so the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a hero is an idol

explanation.surface: A woman's idol is not entirely to be admired.
explanation.definitionFit: The possessive pronoun used for something belonging to a female person, as in her book.

clue.text: Curiosity shown by soldiers in trial cases

indicators.note: the trial encases the soldiers, holding them inside

parts.note: a test is a trial
RE is the Royal Engineers, British army soldiers

explanation.surface: Soldiers are seen with interest in court trials.
explanation.definitionFit: Interest is a feeling of wanting to know more, which is curiosity.

clue.text: All right to pinch a cooker, perhaps? The gall!

indicators.note: pinching something means grabbing it and holding it inside, so one letter goes within the other piece

parts.note: OK means all right
a cooker is a cooking apple, so this is an example of an apple

explanation.surface: Someone protests indignantly at the cheek of a person stealing a stove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooker' suggests a stove, but in Britain a cooker is also a cooking apple. 'The gall!' sounds like outrage at cheek; the definition is the plant growth.
explanation.definitionFit: An oak apple is a round swelling that forms on oak trees where a wasp lays its eggs: a gall.

clue.text: Woman adopting a king's method of self-defence

indicators.note: the woman takes in the letters as one adopts a child into a household

parts.note: Kate is a woman's name
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A woman takes up a king's way of protecting himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Karate is a Japanese martial art of unarmed combat, used for self-protection.

clue.text: Provider of security, one using foil?

definitions.meaning: someone who builds barriers around property, keeping it secure
a swordsman in the sport where a light blunted blade called a foil is used

explanation.walkthrough: 'foil' looks like kitchen wrapping; here it is the fencing sword.
explanation.definitionFit: A fencer both puts up enclosures that protect land and takes part in the sport of swordplay.

clue.text: Leader of the layabouts eating duke's fish

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of the
the layabouts take the letter in, as if swallowing it

parts.note: idlers are layabouts
D is an abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: The chief of a gang of loafers is tucking into a duke's fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The leader is the first letter of 'the', not of 'layabouts'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiddlers are small fish, such as sticklebacks, caught by children in Britain.

clue.text: Unruly bald British ranger, one illegally seizing estate

indicators.note: unruly means disorderly, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: An unruly bald British ranger grabs land that is not his.
explanation.definitionFit: A land-grabber is someone who seizes territory or property unlawfully.

clue.text: Peacekeepers develop wrinkles and ultimately this shambling gait

parts.note: UN, the United Nations, sends peacekeeping forces
to gain is to develop or acquire, as in gaining weight
lines are wrinkles on the face

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word this

explanation.surface: Aging peacekeepers end up walking awkwardly.
explanation.definitionFit: Ungainliness is clumsiness of movement, which a shambling, awkward walk displays.

clue.text: City's diamonds brought in in case by leading lady

indicators.note: the diamonds are brought inside the other piece

parts.note: lest means in case, for fear that
ice is slang for diamonds
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen, the nation's leading lady

explanation.surface: A city's diamonds are packed in a case by the star actress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in case' reads as packing; it means LEST. 'by' puts ER beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Leicester is a city in the English East Midlands.

clue.text: Female journalist beginning to rest on a bishop's throne

parts.note: Cath is a woman's name, short for Catherine
ED is short for editor, a journalist

indicators.note: the beginning of rest is its first letter

explanation.surface: A female reporter starts resting on a bishop's chair.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedra is the official seat of a bishop, giving its name to a cathedral.

clue.text: Heart broken, monarch's touring quiet area of great importance

indicators.note: going round, so the outer letters surround the inner ones
something broken is in pieces, so the letters of heart are rearranged

parts.note: a king is a monarch
sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: A heartbroken king goes on tour round a peaceful region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' is meant as the anagrammed word and the monarch together surrounding the quiet area, with the inserted letters landing between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something earth-shaking is momentous, so significant that it seems to rock the world.

clue.text: Resource a girl's written about in French and Italian

indicators.note: the girl's name is written around the other letters

parts.note: Amy is a girl's name
en is French for in
It is short for Italian, as in It vermouth

explanation.surface: Something useful a girl has written about in French and Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: An amenity is a useful facility or resource, such as a park or library.

clue.text: Prescribed drug Oscar's removed from post

indicators.note: the letter is taken out of the word for post

parts.note: a station is a post where one is stationed
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Oscar is taken off his post because of a prescription drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Statins are cholesterol-lowering medicines commonly prescribed by doctors.

clue.text: Quietly he accepts a pay increase, the hypocrite

parts.note: P stands for piano, the musical direction for quietly

indicators.note: he takes the letters in, holding them inside

parts.note: a rise is a pay increase in British usage

explanation.surface: A man quietly takes a raise, the two-faced fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pharisees were a Jewish sect accused of self-righteousness in the Gospels, so the word means a sanctimonious pretender.

clue.text: Protective garment some initially make fun of

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of some

parts.note: to mock is to make fun of

explanation.surface: A protective overall that some people initially ridicule.
explanation.definitionFit: A smock is a loose overall worn over clothes to keep them clean.

clue.text: English carrier losing right to deliver game

indicators.note: the carrier loses a letter, which is dropped from the word

parts.note: a carter is someone who carries goods by cart

explanation.surface: An English delivery firm fails to deliver a parcel after losing its rights.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecarte is a nineteenth-century card game for two players.

clue.text: Fuss about an enlisted man moving very slowly

indicators.note: the fuss goes round the other letters

parts.note: ado means fuss, as in much ado
A is the indefinite article, a form of an
a GI is an American enlisted soldier

explanation.surface: A fuss is made over a soldier who is dawdling.
explanation.definitionFit: Adagio is the musical tempo marking for playing slowly and gracefully.

clue.text: Odd parts of global state

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters, first, third and fifth, of global

explanation.surface: Uneven pieces of a world state.
explanation.definitionFit: Goa is a small state on the west coast of India.

clue.text: Popular instrument half of team used to put cannula in

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
a tuba is a brass instrument

indicators.note: half of team means its first two letters

explanation.surface: A popular tuba player takes half the team to hospital for a drip.
explanation.definitionFit: To intubate is to insert a tube into a patient, such as a breathing tube or cannula.

clue.text: A bird originally encountered in this writer's nonsense

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the word for this writer's

parts.note: my is what the writer would say of their own things
a lark is a songbird

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of encountered

explanation.surface: A bird I came across features in my rubbish writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Malarkey is an informal word for meaningless talk, or rubbish.

clue.text: Eager group of artists?

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts
a ring is a group of people, such as a smuggling ring

explanation.surface: A painters' collective is described as keen.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a cryptic definition, but 'of' just links group and artists, joined artists first.
explanation.definitionFit: Raring, as in raring to go, means very keen and impatient to start.
